mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 9.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 9.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases (i.e., when both series decline, returns are positive in >55% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of industrial production contraction (INDPRO below 100), manufacturing output slowdowns lead to reduced corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index level above 220 (CPIAUCSL > 220) indicates a high cumulative inflation environment, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 220.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (as measured by GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth is above 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of sustained job growth (PAYEMS exceeding 120,000 thousand), labor market strength supports consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 120000.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index above 102.0 signals strong manufacturing activity, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 102.0.
